theme: Opposition; the Temple completed; Passover kept
readingInstruction: Read Ezra 4:1-6:22. Enemies stop the work for about fifteen years, and God uses two prophets to restart it. The temple is finished, and the people keep the Passover. Read for the way opposition is met.
settingTheScene: The neighbors of the returning Jews, resettled peoples of the former northern kingdom, offered to help build the temple. When Zerubbabel and Jeshua refused, they became enemies. They discouraged the builders, bribed officials, and finally wrote letters to the Persian court. The work stopped from about 536 to 520 BC. Haggai and Zechariah, whom you will read near the end of this unit, then preached, and the work resumed. The temple was finished in 516 BC, seventy years after its destruction.
observation: “You have nothing to do with us in building a house to our God” (4:3).
“Then the people of the land discouraged the people of Judah and made them afraid to build” (4:4).
“Then the work on the house of God in Jerusalem stopped” (4:24).
“Then the prophets, Haggai and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews” (5:1).
“But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they were not stopped” (5:5).
“We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the house that was built many years ago” (5:11).
“And the elders of the Jews built and prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet” (6:14).
“And they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with joy, for the LORD had made them joyful” (6:22).
interpretation:
The conflict begins with an offer that sounds friendly. The local peoples say, “Let us build with you, for we worship your God.” Zerubbabel refuses. It was not unkind but wise. These people had mixed the worship of the LORD with other gods (2 Kings 17:33). To build together would have meant a compromised temple. The refusal cost them, because opposition followed: discouragement, fear, bribes, and accusations. Tactics of those who oppose God’s work have not changed.

The work stops. For sixteen years, the foundation sits unfinished. The people turn to their own homes. This is a lesson in how a good beginning can stall when we are tired, afraid, or distracted.

But God sends help. Haggai and Zechariah prophesy, and the leaders rise and start building again. When the governor Tattenai asks who authorized them, the Jews answer with confidence and with their history: “We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth.” A letter is sent to Darius, and he discovers the original decree of Cyrus in the archives. He not only allows the work but orders the provinces to pay for it. The enemies who tried to stop it are made to fund it.

The note in 5:5 is the heart of it: “The eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they were not stopped.” God is watching. The temple is finished in the sixth year of Darius, and the dedication is full of joy. They keep the Passover, as in Hezekiah’s and Josiah’s days. And the writer adds: “The LORD had made them joyful, and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them.” Even the opposition was in God’s hand.
connection: Jesus said, “I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (Matthew 16:18). Nehemiah and Paul faced similar opposition (Acts 19, 2 Corinthians 11). 1 Peter 2:5 says we are being built up as a spiritual house. Galatians 6:9 says, “Let us not grow weary of doing good.” Philippians 4:6: do not be anxious. Romans 8:31: if God is for us, who can be against us?
application:
Think about a project God gave you that has stalled. Ask what is needed to start again.

Pray for those who face opposition in their ministry or work.

Be discerning about offers of “help” that would compromise your devotion to God.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to keep you building when you are afraid or tired.
Thank him that his eye is on those who serve him.
Ask him to raise up encouragers around you.
